claims.text: The identity of X controls whether CrFeCoNiX develops a stable, coherent protective oxide scale above 900 °C.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form a slow-growing Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer on Al-containing alloys is adherent.
Al2O3 minimizes stress at the alloy-oxide interface.
Al2O3 acts as an effective oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Al2O3 has favorable lattice matching with the Al-containing CrFeCoNi alloy substrate.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form rapidly growing manganese oxides.
The manganese oxides are non-coherent and develop high growth stresses.
High stresses in the manganese-oxide scale cause cracking and spallation.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form a silicate interlayer.
The silicate interlayer provides protection intermediate between the Al- and Mn-containing alloys.
Element-specific oxygen affinity determines the initial surface oxide phase.
Al-containing alloys maintain a stable, coherent, self-healing protective scale under the specified high-temperature exposures.
Mn-containing alloys develop unstable, cracked, and spalling scales under the same exposures.
Si-containing alloys exhibit oxide morphology and protection intermediate between those of the Al- and Mn-containing alloys.
The predicted alloy-dependent behavior applies primarily to well-homogenized, single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys may introduce additional oxidation complexities.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary specify exposure above 900 °C, whereas the stated test range is 900–1000 °C and therefore includes 900 °C, which is not above 900 °C.
